decisions.reason: The existing same-message migration correctly replaces separate-board framing, but its normal-operation role accidentally omits the previously included SK6812 LEDs despite the client's requirement to preserve functionality.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: I was thinking, if you have time for a new project and are willing to do it, that we try to make as cheap as possible single board for this project. So everything will be on one board and from start we try to match JLCPCB Basica component (as much as possible). It will have much less connectors as there are no interboard connectors. Also if you have some idea on how to make something better/cheaper but have same functionality you can suggest. I can add it as new milestone to this project and we can agree on price. What do you think does it make sense?

value_updates.normal_operation_role: Primary source for the ESP32-S3, INA219, downstream 3.3V sensors, I2C display, TTP223, AM312, and SK6812 addressable LEDs in the single integrated-board architecture
value_updates.voltage_compensation_purpose: Compensate for the integrated-board Schottky-diode OR-ing drop so the system rail remains at 3.3V under all conditions

decisions.reason: The single integrated-board architecture makes the Main Board scope and the board-specific LED-interconnect description stale; the source does not establish whether that JST connector remains, so the obsolete key must be removed rather than replaced speculatively.
